title: Function Contract
definition: A function contract states accepted inputs, preconditions, promised outputs or postconditions, observable effects, and failure behavior.
purpose: Make caller and function responsibilities explicit before implementation details are chosen.
history: Preconditions and postconditions connect program specification, Hoare-style reasoning, and design by contract.
mental_model: The caller promises the precondition; if it holds, the function promises the postcondition or documented failure behavior.
analogy: A delivery agreement; it fails when software effects, timing, aliasing, or partial failure are omitted from the agreement.
common_mistakes: Leaving hidden inputs or effects unstated
industry_notes: Contracts may be expressed through types, documentation, assertions, tests, schemas, or combinations; no single notation is sufficient in every system.
ai_notes: Ask AI to separate assumptions from guarantees and identify unexpressed dependencies.
interview_notes: Ask who owns a violated precondition and how postconditions become testable.
